about.title: About us
about.body1: For decades we have opened our home to animals in distress, giving them a place to live. We started by sterilizing abandoned cats, then took in dogs, and later also welcomed elderly horses.
about.body2: Our sanctuary kept growing until the spring of 2019, when we found ourselves on the edge of financial collapse. A young pony named Inaya became very ill and had to be hospitalized twice. She needed costly treatment and food, which put us under serious financial strain. The high cost of caring for Inaya put the continuity of our work at risk and made us realize we could no longer bear the care of every animal alone. That's why we set up our association, to be supported in our mission. Thanks to Inaya, we understood that this project needed to be shared with many animal lovers — which is why our association carries her name.
about.body3: Today we carry on our passion for rescuing and caring for animals in distress. We are working hard to expand our sanctuary and welcome more animals in need, offering them a peaceful haven to grow old in.

adopt.title: Adopting at Inaya
adopt.intro: Would you like to adopt a dog or cat at Inaya?
steps: You call +33 6 11 50 13 17 to set up an appointment to visit the animals. The sanctuary has no regular opening hours and hosts visits by appointment only.
You fall in love and would like to reserve an animal to adopt.
You fill out a "commitment and awareness certificate", which requires you to think carefully — at least one week — before adopting.

During that week, a volunteer from INAYA will visit you to discuss your adoption plan and check whether your home is suitable for the animal of your choice. The volunteer gives us their opinion on whether to accept or decline your application.
After approval, you make another appointment to sign the adoption contract, pay the adoption fee, and pick up the animal. Bring a copy of your ID and proof of address to complete your file.

About a month later, a volunteer makes a follow-up visit to check that everything is going well. If so, the adoption is validated and the microchip transferred to your name. If you decide to return the animal, there is no refund.
The shelter reserves the right to carry out an unannounced follow-up visit, and to remove an animal if it is in danger.
If you can no longer care for the animal, you are required to return it to the sanctuary. Transferring it to a third party or rehoming it via social media is not allowed.
adopt.dogPricingNote: All animals are microchipped, dewormed, vaccinated (at least an initial round) and sterilized, plus 2025 membership included.
adopt.catPricingNote: All cats are microchipped, dewormed, vaccinated (at least an initial round), sterilized and tested for FIV/FeLV, plus 2025 membership included.
adopt.unsterilizedNote: If the animal isn't sterilized yet at the time of adoption, you'll receive a certificate of coverage from INAYA — with this document, sterilization at our veterinary clinic is free once the animal is old enough.

calicivirus.title: Adopting a cat with calicivirus
calicivirus.intro: Feline calicivirosis is part of cat flu (coryza syndrome). It affects some of our residents, without stopping them from living a wonderful life with a loving family.
calicivirus.whatText: Feline calicivirus (FCV) cannot be transmitted to humans. It spreads only between cats, mainly through oral, nasal or eye secretions, and by contact with contaminated surfaces.
calicivirus.symptomsIntro: These cats may experience flare-ups throughout their lives:
symptoms: Mouth ulcers and gingivitis, which can cause difficulty eating and weight loss
calicivirus.treatmentText: There is currently no effective antiviral treatment for calicivirus. Treatment therefore focuses on improving the cat's comfort and limiting complications. With good follow-up care, a cat with chronic calicivirosis can live for several years.
calicivirus.careText: Adopting a cat with calicivirus is a true act of kindness. The shelter covers calicivirus-related veterinary costs for 6 months from the adoption date.
calicivirus.closing: They are all affectionate and just waiting for one thing: a wonderful family for life.

surrender.title: Surrendering an animal
surrender.intro: Do you need to give up your animal?
surrender.waitlistNote: Our sanctuary is often full because of the large number of rescues, emergencies and unexpected arrivals — for this reason, there is a waiting list of indefinite length.
surrender.conditionsTitle: To surrender a dog or cat, several conditions apply:
conditions: The animal is identified (microchip or tattoo) in the name of the person surrendering it. If the owner has passed away, a copy of the death certificate is required.

You have the I-CAD identification card (blue A4 document), which you must sign on the back when surrendering the animal. If this document is missing, we will draw up a surrender certificate along with a copy of your ID.

The surrender fee is €180 for a sterilized dog and €100 for a sterilized cat. This contribution helps the shelter feed and care for your animal (deworming, vaccination, flea treatment, Seresto collar, etc.), whether it stays with us for a short time or for years. If the animal isn't sterilized, the fee is doubled, since sterilization will be carried out here on intake by our veterinary clinic.

volunteer.title: Join us
volunteer.intro: Being a volunteer with us is far more than giving a little of your time. It's choosing to be there for those who cannot speak, who have sometimes known abandonment, fear or loneliness. It's sharing values of solidarity, mutual support and respect, and understanding that every gesture, even the simplest, matters. Because at the sanctuary, it isn't only cuddles, tender looks and moments of connection.
volunteer.dailyLifeBody: There's also the everyday work. Cleaning the enclosures. Picking up waste. Disinfecting. Carrying, washing, repairing. Preparing meals, handing out food, changing the water. Maintaining fences. Starting over, day after day. These are physical, repetitive tasks — sometimes hard and often messy. But behind each one, there's an animal sleeping somewhere clean, eating its fill, drinking fresh water, able to live in a healthy, safe environment. Being a volunteer means accepting to get your hands dirty to give them a better life.
volunteer.closingBody: It's giving your energy when you're tired. It's showing up even when it's raining. It's sometimes doing things no one sees, but that concretely change the animals' lives. Because caring for them isn't just about loving them. It's taking care of them, every day — even in the least glamorous tasks. A few hours a week, one day now and then, or more… it doesn't matter. Every presence counts. Every gesture counts. Every helping hand counts. And maybe, at the end of that tiring day, when you meet their gaze, you'll understand why you did it:
conditions: You'd like to give your time to animals in distress
You follow health protocols and safety rules
You understand that volunteering at a shelter is demanding work, physically, mentally and emotionally
You commit to at least one morning a week (8:30am – 12:30pm)

fosterFamily.title: Foster family
fosterFamily.intro: Becoming a foster family means offering an animal a temporary home during a convalescence or while waiting for a permanent adoption, while staying in touch with our team.
fosterFamily.roleTitle: The role of a foster family
role: Temporarily house an animal during a convalescence or before its adoption
Socialize it and help it adjust to home life
Keep us informed of its behavior and health
Introduce it to prospective adopters with our agreement
fosterFamily.conditionsTitle: Conditions to become a foster family
conditions: Have housing suited to the animal you're hosting (a fenced garden for a dog, a secure space for a cat…)
Be able to handle the necessary trips to our partner veterinarian
Accept follow-up visits and stay in regular contact with the association
Veterinary and food costs can be covered by the association

help.title: Help us
help.intro: As a non-profit organization, we are constantly looking for funding to keep caring for our animals. Most of our funds go toward daily food for all the animals — hay, dry food, supplements — and the upkeep of pastures. There are also fixed medical costs such as sterilization and castration, deworming products, and flea and tick prevention. Then there are cleaning and disinfecting supplies, dental care, and hoof care. And on top of that, there are sometimes heavy, unexpected costs in case of illness or accident. The list is long.

gift.text: Make a one-time donation that helps secure our near future.

sponsorship.title: Sponsorship
sponsorship.text: You can sponsor a specific animal by becoming its godparent. Browse the list on our "Our animals" page and choose a fixed monthly amount. Your name will appear on the animal's passport, and every year you'll receive news and photos of your godchild.

adoption.title: Adoption
adoption.text: Sometimes we look for adoptive families. Since our sanctuary has limited space, some animals cannot stay indefinitely. Adoption candidates are screened and pay a contribution that benefits the animals who remain.

teaming.title: €1 a month to support the sanctuary
teaming.intro: What if just €1 a month could make a real difference for animals in distress? That's only €12 a year — your gift on Teaming helps the sanctuary cover care, medication, hospital stays, and everything our animals need for their well-being.
teaming.flyerAlt: "Join our Teaming network" flyer: €1 a month to save lives, with the link and QR code to the fundraiser.

step1.title: 1. Head to Teaming
step1.text: Go to the Teaming website, the platform that manages donations for good causes.

step2.title: 2. Create your account
step2.text: Signing up is quick and free.

step3.title: 3. Choose our project
step3.text: Select "Sanctuaire / Refuge INAYA pour les animaux en détresse".

step4.title: 4. It's charged monthly
step4.text: Your account is then charged €1 a month, automatically — no further steps needed.

teaming.impactTitle: A few euros each, an enormous help for them
teaming.impactBody1: Our posts and reels reach a huge number of people: on September 4, a video of two puppies arriving in critical condition reached 182,868 views — one of the two sadly didn't survive. On December 31, our post about the typhus outbreak reached 15,585 views, a crisis that brought heavy vet bills: medication, hospital stays, care, cremations.
teaming.impactBody2: Despite those thousands of views and likes, only 24 people joined us on Teaming this summer. We're convinced we can be many more: imagine if hundreds, or thousands, of people supported us with just €1 a month.
teaming.ctaTitle: Ready to join us on Teaming?
teaming.ctaText: Behind that small euro lies care, medication, meals, hospital stays — and above all, one more chance for the animals we take in.
